events.text: You build a sky over {pw_world}. Not the blue one: that was always there. This one is a floor of cloud with a court on it, {pw_heaven}, and a long stair of light down to the highest mountain. The priests below look up and, for the first time, see somewhere to go.

choices.text: Set the first lamp in its hall yourself

effects.log: The lamp burns without oil. Below, every temple of {pw_world} lights at the same moment, and nobody can say why.

choices.text: Leave its halls empty for the gods to come

effects.log: You leave the halls of {pw_heaven} bare and open. A heaven, you think, should be filled by the ones who earn it.

events.text: {pw_lgod} climbs the stair of light with bare feet and stands before you in {pw_heaven}, shaking a little. You give them {pw_ldomain} to keep. In {pw_world} the first shrine to them goes up before the year is out, and it is a little crooked, and they love it more than anything.

choices.text: Tell them what you expect of a god

effects.log: You tell {pw_lgod} that a god is a servant who is never thanked enough. They bow very low and do not argue.

choices.text: Tell them they were chosen because they were kind

effects.log: {pw_lgod} weeps, briefly, in the hall of heaven. Then they go down to look at their crooked shrine again.

events.text: Out of the morning mist of {pw_world} walk {pw_lpeople}, blinking, holding hands, carrying the first tools you thought of for them. The peoples who were there before watch from the hills, not sure yet whether these are neighbours or trouble. Everyone in the world, old and new, looks up at the sky.

choices.text: Give them a first song

effects.log: {pw_lpeople} sing it all the way to the river. By the third verse the older peoples are humming along.

choices.text: Give them a first law: welcome the stranger

effects.log: {pw_lpeople} carve your law over their first gate. It will not always be kept, but it will always be there.

events.text: {pw_lbeast} goes down into {pw_world} and climbs to its highest mountain, turns three times, and lies down with its head on its paws to watch the valleys. The shepherds below leave it the first milk of every spring. It pretends not to notice.

choices.text: Tell it what it guards

effects.log: You tell {pw_lbeast} the names of the valleys, one by one. It listens to every one.

choices.text: Tell it to guard them even from you

effects.log: {pw_lbeast} looks up at you for a long moment, then nods. A guardian that would guard against its maker is a real one.

events.text: In {pw_world} a child climbs onto the back of {pw_lbeast} for a dare, and is not thrown. By the end of the generation whole caravans ride them. The roads grow longer, the kingdoms bolder, and every people of the world has a new word for far away that means a little less than it used to.

choices.text: Bless the first rider

effects.log: The first rider of {pw_world} is remembered in every song of the road. They never knew a god was watching.

choices.text: Teach the beasts to come home

effects.log: Lost riders of {pw_world} learn to let go of the reins. {pw_lbeast} always knows the way back.

events.text: You let {pw_lbeast} loose in the wild places of {pw_world}. The first village it passes is empty by noon, every soul fled to the temples, and all night the prayers rise to you, the same prayer said in a thousand voices: save us. You do not. Not yet. Somewhere down there a hero has to find out what they are.

choices.text: Watch for the one who stands up

effects.log: You watch {pw_world} closely. It is hard. You keep your hands still.

choices.text: Send the villages a warning dream

effects.log: Every elder of {pw_world} dreams of the beast the night before it comes. Fewer people are where it walks.

events.text: On clear nights in {pw_world} you can see it: a faint second sky above the stars, with lamps in it. The old people call it {pw_heaven} and say the gods live there, and that the one who made the world sits at the top of the stair and never sleeps. You look at it for a long time.

choices.text: Climb the highest hill to see it better

effects.log: From the hill the lamps of {pw_heaven} are brighter. You think one of them flickers, as if someone passed in front of it.

choices.text: Make a wish on the second sky

effects.log: You wish, a little embarrassed. Nobody answers. You feel, all the same, that it was heard.

events.text: The village keeps a small shrine to {pw_lgod}, the god of {pw_ldomain}, with a carved face worn smooth by hands. The priest says {pw_lgod} was once a person of this world like you, and climbed the stair of light, and remembers what it is to be cold and hungry. That is why people pray to them first.

choices.text: Leave an offering of bread

effects.log: You leave the bread. In the morning it is gone. The priest says birds; you are not so sure.

choices.text: Ask the priest how a person becomes a god

effects.log: The priest laughs and says: by being chosen. Then, more quietly: and by being worth choosing.

events.text: Market day brings people from all the peoples of {pw_world}: tall ones, quiet ones, ones with songs you do not know. A stall-keeper of {pw_lpeople} sells you a cup of something hot and asks which people you are. You tell them. "Ah," they say, "the god made you first. Or last. I forget which."

choices.text: Ask about their people

effects.log: They talk for an hour about their grandmother, their river and their gods. You leave with a new friend and an empty cup.

choices.text: Trade them a story for the cup

effects.log: Your story is about the god who made the world. They have heard a different version. You argue happily until dusk.

events.text: There is war between two peoples of {pw_world}, and it has come close enough that the road is full of carts going the other way. A family of the other side asks for water at your door. Their eldest watches you, waiting to see what kind of person you are.

choices.text: Give them water and bread

effects.log: They drink and eat and go on. Years later the eldest comes back to thank you, after the peace.

choices.text: Give them water, and keep the door shut

effects.log: They drink and go. You tell yourself it was enough. Some nights you are not sure.

events.text: Every spring the shepherds take the first milk up the mountain to {pw_lbeast}, the guardian of {pw_world}, and this year you carry the pail. At the top it is lying in the sun, enormous and old and patient, and it opens one eye and looks at you as if it has always known you.

choices.text: Kneel and set the pail down

effects.log: The guardian drinks, and breathes on you once, warm as a summer wind. The shepherds say that means a long life.

choices.text: Ask it, quietly, if it remembers its maker

effects.log: The guardian looks at you for a long time. Then it lays its great head down next to you, and does not move until dusk.

events.text: Everyone in {pw_world} learns to ride {pw_lbeast} sooner or later, and this is your year. The one they give you is old and wise and has opinions about the road. The stable master says it has carried kings and children and once a priest who fell asleep for three days, and never lost one of them.

choices.text: Ride it out to the edge of the land

effects.log: You ride until the land runs out. The beast stands with you at the edge a while, then turns for home without being asked.

choices.text: Let it choose the road

effects.log: It takes you somewhere you would never have gone: a valley of white flowers nobody seems to know about.

events.text: {pw_lbeast} has come down out of the wild places of {pw_world} at last, to the river below your village. The temples have prayed for a year and the god has not answered. The elders are packing. Somebody, says the oldest of them, looking at nobody, ought to go down to the river.

choices.text: Go down to the river and face it

ok.log: You go down to the river. It is the longest day of your life. At dusk the beast lies still in the shallows, and the village comes down to stare at you.

fail.log: You go down to the river and are thrown into it. You crawl out half drowned. The beast does not even look back.

choices.text: Lead the village up into the hills

effects.log: You lead them up into the hills, the old ones first. Nobody is lost. Someone else will have to be the hero.

choices.text: Pray to the god who made the world

effects.log: You pray all night. You have the strange feeling that somewhere far above, someone is trying very hard not to answer.
